h: פָּרָשַׁת הַחֹדֶשׁ, מַאֲמָר ב׳ Parshas HaChodesh — Maamar Bais

p: רִאשׁוֹן הוּא לָכֶם וְגוֹמֵר [שְׁמוֹת יב, ב]
it is first for you" etc. (Shemos 12:2).
for 'head' and 'first' are still to come.
That is, Nevuchadnetzar is "head" in the kelipah,
corresponding to the attribute of Chochmah in holiness —
which is the beginning of recognition.
"the one killed, the other sought to kill;
the one destroyed, the other sought to destroy"
And opposite what is in holiness —
sought to kill and destroy everything.
And "first" is the kelipah of Esav,
which corresponded to the attribute of Keser Elyon,
which is hidden from all thought.
And so, as its counterpart, his power was
to conceal himself so that he could mislead,
as we find with Yitzchak Avinu,
that Esav would "trap him with his mouth":
he would say, "In the beis midrash —
(as it says in Midrash Tanchuma, Toldos 8).
And certainly Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
how to distinguish between truth and falsehood;
"He appeared to him as a talmid chacham,
דְּאָמַר מָר הַמְהַלֵּךְ לִימִין רַבּוֹ כּוּלֵּי
for Mar said: one who walks at his teacher's right" etc.;
until he appeared to Yaakov like his teacher
who shows him the good path.
And so regarding the future it is stated
He wraps himself in his tallis like an elder
וּבָא וְיוֹשֵׁב לוֹ אֵצֶל יַעֲקֹב כּוּלֵּי
and comes and sits beside Yaakov" etc.;
for this is his power, that he can conceal himself
And about this it is said (Ovadiah 1:4):
"And if your nest is set among the stars,
from there I will bring you down, says Hashem" —
for Hashem Yisbarach, who judges the hearts,
will bring him down to earth.
And it is written right after that (ibid. 1:6):
the hidden places of his heart, which is full of abomination.
And so the first exile was
"The earlier ones, whose sin was revealed";
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁאָז הָיָה טְעָנוֹת עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
that is, then there were claims against Yisrael
for they transgressed the words of the Torah
Not so in the Second Temple era,
when they were engaged in Torah and mitzvos
only there was a claim against them over hidden matters.
And this is the kelipah of Esav and Amalek,
as they said in the holy Zohar
out of doubt — whether he knows or does not know —
and Hashem Yisbarach, who loves justice,
when there is an accuser, executes judgment;
and therefore the second exile was
And this is what they said:
even though the main renewal of the moon
is the light of Torah, not deeds.
But the essence of the light of Torah
Only, we have already said many times
"in your mouth and in your heart, to do it,"
and it does not say "in your deeds,"
for the completion of the deed comes from Hashem Yisbarach
(וְנִתְבָּאֵר פְּקוּדֵי מַאֲמָר ג עַיֵּין שָׁם בַּאֲרִיכוּת)
(and it was explained in Pekudei, maamar 3; see there at length).
And this is what they said, "Renew your deeds":
that is, through the renewal of light
and from this one will come to deeds,
for the completion of the deed
And so it is related of the Yid HaKadosh,
may his memory be for a blessing for the life of the World to Come,
that he said that on this Shabbos
there is a renewal in abundance
"This month shall be for you the head of months" —
שֶׁכָּל חֹדֶשׁ יֵשׁ לוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת
for each month has its own particular holiness,
and the first day is called Rosh Chodesh,
for it is the head of the whole month,
and it contains all the holiness of the month.
And Nissan contains all the holiness
and so its Rosh Chodesh is called
indicating that they are bound to the root,
opposite the kelipah of Bavel and Esav,
the two exiles, as mentioned above.
all the holiness of the weekdays that follow it;
and when Rosh Chodesh Nissan falls on Shabbos,
an abundance of renewal in words of Torah.

paragraphs.text: Pesikta Rabbasi 15, conclusion, HaChodesh — “Rabbi Berechyah said in Rabbi Yitzchak's name: This month—renew your deeds, for head and first are still to come. Head is the wicked Nevuchadnezzar, of whom it is written, You are the head of gold. First is the wicked Esav, of whom it is written, The first came out. Who will exact payment for you? The First: I, Hashem, am first, and with the last I am He.” The Midrash sets the two hostile firsts against God, the First. Rav Tzadok distinguishes overt opposition to revealed wisdom from a concealed claim against Israel's inward character.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 11a — “Achasheverosh: Rav said, The brother of the head, and the counterpart of the head. Brother of the head means brother of wicked Nevuchadnezzar, who is called head: You are the head of gold. His counterpart: the one killed, and the other sought to kill; the one destroyed, and the other sought to destroy, as it is said, In the reign of Achasheverosh, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Yehudah and Jerusalem.” The comparison is one of destructive intention and action. Rav Tzadok places both kings opposite holy wisdom, through which the earth is founded.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Rashi on Bereishis 25:27 — “‘Who knew trapping’: to trap and deceive his father with his mouth, asking him, ‘Father, how does one tithe salt and straw?’ so that his father thought he was meticulous in mitzvos.” Rashi shows what the hiding looked like. Esav dressed himself in the finest points of halachah, the very form of a ben Torah.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Vayigash 4 — “Yitzchak wished to draw Esav close because Esav had the choice, being called ‘a Yisrael who is a mumar,’ and it hung in the balance whether he could enter the holiness of Yisrael.” The Gemara cited there is Kiddushin 18a. This adds to Rav Tzadok’s point. Yitzchak was not simply fooled. Esav’s concealment worked on a real potential in him, which is why it could not be seen through.

paragraphs.text: Yoma 9b — “The second Temple: they occupied themselves with Torah, commandments, and acts of kindness. Why was it destroyed? Because it contained baseless hatred. This teaches that baseless hatred is equivalent to the three transgressions of idolatry, forbidden relations, and bloodshed. ... Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar both said: The earlier ones, whose sin was revealed, had the end of their exile revealed; the later ones, whose sin was not revealed, did not have their end revealed.” The Gemara contrasts visible religious achievement with destructive hatred and the differing revelation of the exile's end. Rav Tzadok links this inward failure with the concealed opposition of Edom.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 27a — “Perhaps study is different, because study leads to action. Marriage too is different: He did not create it for emptiness; He formed it to be inhabited. But exchanging Torah for Torah may not be permitted.” The discussion concerns selling a Torah scroll to enable study or marriage. Rav Tzadok draws from its reason for preferring study the principle that renewal in Torah must bear fruit in action.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Pekudei 3 — “It says ‘in your mouth and in your heart to do it,’ not ‘in your deeds,’ for the completion of the deed is from Hashem, who asks of us only the desire of the heart.” This is the passage Rav Tzadok refers to here. It adds the Zohar source (III 160a). It also shows why “renew your deeds” begins with renewed Torah in the heart.
